title: Scala Spark RDD error : java.lang.ClassCastException: cannot assign instance of java.lang.invoke.SerializedLambda
question:
I am a beginner to Scala and Spark.

scala version : 2.12.10

spark version : 3.0.1

I'm trying a very simple spark rdd function in scala.

But I get an error.

(1) build.sbt


scalaVersion := "2.12.10"


name := "hello-world"
organization := "ch.epfl.scala"
version := "1.0"


libraryDependencies += "org.scala-lang.modules" %% "scala-parser-combinators" % "1.1.2"
libraryDependencies +=        "org.apache.spark" %% "spark-sql" % "3.0.1" 
libraryDependencies +=        "org.apache.spark" %% "spark-core" % "3.0.1"

(2) Main.scala

import org.apache.spark.sql.SparkSession
object Main extends App {
  println("Hello, World!")

  implicit val spark = SparkSession.builder()
        .master("spark://centos-master:7077")
        // .master("local[*]")
        .appName("spark-api")
        .getOrCreate()


  val inputrdd = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(Seq(("arth",10), ("arth", 20), ("samuel", 60), ("jack", 65)))
      println("inputrdd : ", inputrdd)
  val mapped = inputrdd.mapValues(x => (x, 1))
  println("mapped : ", mapped)
  mapped.collect.foreach(println)
}

It seems that an error occurs in the mapped.collect.foreach(println) part.

If I need more libraries or if the code is wrong (but it works fine in spark-shell)....

How to solve it?
answer:
simply jar is missing we need to supply explicitly either by spark-submit like this

spark-submit \
  --class your.main.Class \
  --master spark://centos-master:7077 \
  --jars yourdependency1.jar,yourdependency2.jar \
  your-application.jar

or by your code above code

import org.apache.spark.sql.SparkSession

object MyApp {
  def main(args: Array[String]): Unit = {
    val spark = SparkSession.builder()
      .master("spark://centos-master:7077")
      .appName("spark-api")
      .getOrCreate()

    // Add JAR dynamically
    spark.sparkContext.addJar("yourdependency1.jar")
    spark.sparkContext.addJar("yourdependency2.jar")

    // Now your RDD/DataFrame operations can use classes in these JARs
    val rdd = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(Seq(1,2,3))
    println(rdd.collect().mkString(","))
  }
}
